title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Are we just checking whether any number appears more than once?
teacher_message:
nums: [x] → [y] → [x]
       0     1     2

Yes—your interpretation is right: if the same value occurs at least twice in nums, the condition is true.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner is checking whether the task asks if any value appears more than once.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question seeking confirmation, not a demonstrated explanation of the duplicate condition.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: So I could just compare each number with the one right before it, right?
teacher_message:
nums: [x] → [y] → [x]
       0     1     2

Not quite—comparing only with the immediately previous value can miss a duplicate separated by other values. The condition is true whenever any value appears at least twice anywhere in nums. In this trace, which positions contain the duplicate?

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner limits duplicate detection to immediately adjacent values.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question proposing a local comparison, not an explanation that any value appearing at least twice satisfies the condition.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: The duplicate is x at positions 0 and 2, even though y is between them.
teacher_message:
nums: [x] → [y] → [x]
       0     1     2

Correct—the x values at positions 0 and 2 show that x appears at least twice in nums. That satisfies the duplicate condition.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner traces nums and identifies the repeated value across nonadjacent positions.

model_assessment.evidence_quote: The duplicate is x at positions 0 and 2, even though y is between them.
model_assessment.rationale: The learner identifies a value appearing at least twice despite separation by another value.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Do I need to remember every number I’ve already seen?
teacher_message:
nums: [x] → [y] → [x]
       0     1     2
box before num: {}   {x}   {x, y}

Keep the distinct values in box. Add num when it is not there; when num is already in box, return true immediately.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Asks whether previously seen values must be retained.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question and does not demonstrate how previously seen values are maintained.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: I think I check the box first, but I’m not sure if I add the number before checking.
teacher_message:
nums: [x] → [y] → [x]
       0     1     2
box before num: {}   {x}   {x, y}

Check first. If num is not in box, add it; if num is already in box, return true immediately. For the final x, box is {x, y}, so return true. Which action happens first: checking or adding?

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner is unsure whether membership checking or insertion comes first.

model_assessment.rationale: The message expresses uncertainty about operation order but does not demonstrate the seen-values invariant.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: Checking happens first, then I add the number only if it isn’t already in the box.
teacher_message:
nums: [x] → [y] → [x]
       0     1     2
box before num: {}   {x}   {x, y}

Exactly: check whether num is in box first. If it is not, add num to box and continue; if it is already there, return true immediately. For the final num = x, box = {x, y}, so the duplicate is detected.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Recognizes the check-before-add rule for seen values.

model_assessment.evidence_quote: Checking happens first, then I add the number only if it isn’t already in the box.
model_assessment.rationale: The learner correctly states that membership is checked before adding a new value.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: If I finish the list without finding a repeat, do I return false?

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Asks about the no-duplicate endpoint without stating the check-before-add procedure.

model_assessment.rationale: The message asks for confirmation about returning false after a full scan but does not demonstrate checking membership before adding.

title: Contains Duplicate
problem: Return true if any value appears at least twice in nums.
learner_message: So if the first number is unique, I can return false right away?

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Confuses a unique first value with completing the full scan without finding duplicates.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner proposes returning false after checking only the first number, which does not demonstrate checking all values.
